_comment: Cases for tools/diff_harness.py.
TWO KINDS OF CASE:
parity    - fired at BOTH backends, status + full body diffed field by
field. The gate wherever the port intends to match legacy.
contract  - any of expect_status/expect_absent/expect_present is set.
Fired at the PORT ONLY and asserted against the expectation.
For `aiservices` (rewritten, not ported) and for the security
invariants, where legacy is wrong and parity would demand the
bug back. These keep working after legacy is deleted.
SAFETY: these fire at two backends sharing ONE database. Every case here is
read-only or is rejected before it writes. Do not add a case that creates,
updates or deletes: it would be applied twice and mutate a real instance.
IDENTIFIERS: never hardcode one. Use ${resource_id} etc. and declare it in
`fixtures` below - a hardcoded id survives a --reset as a 404-vs-404 PASS
that tests nothing. An unresolved fixture SKIPS its cases; it never falls
back to a literal.
Case keys:
name/method/path/query/body/form/headers/auth/ignore  as before
expect_status    contract: the status the PORT must return
expect_absent    contract: key names that must appear NOWHERE, any depth
expect_present   contract: key names that must appear somewhere
Volatile values (_id, createdAt, token, task_id, ...) are replaced with a
type marker globally, so they never cause false failures.

fixtures.name: type_slugs
fixtures.covers: every listing and search case - they must name content types this instance actually has

fixtures.name: resource_id
fixtures.covers: every resource detail, article, images, child-record and public-mirror case

fixtures.name: public_resource_id
fixtures.covers: every anonymous resource and record case - a resource the AUTHENTICATED listing returns is not necessarily public, and pointing an anonymous case at one tests refusal while looking like it tests the response

fixtures.name: public_record_id
fixtures.covers: the public record detail, page-viewer and transcription cases - the record is reached THROUGH a public resource, so its whole ancestry is public by construction

fixtures.name: record_id
fixtures.covers: record detail, viewers, transcription, metadata and the public record mirror

fixtures.name: image_record_id
fixtures.covers: the image reader - `ImageViewer.tsx` fetches an image through the DOCUMENT reader's two routes, so an image record must be servable by both

fixtures.name: view_id
fixtures.covers: view detail and its file counts - an instance with no views cannot exercise these

fixtures.name: provider_id
fixtures.covers: every per-provider read - the detail, the model catalogue and the reachability check, which is where a stored credential would surface if it ever escaped
fixtures._note: Resolved from the PORT because aiservices was rewritten: legacy answers this route with a bare array of vendor NAMES, so no extract can read an id out of both. Feeds contract cases only - the harness refuses at load time if a parity case borrows it.

cases.name: health: readiness
_note: Error strings are driver-specific text and the two stacks reach the same
services through different client wrappers, so the wording can differ
legitimately. The status ('ok'/'error'/'disabled') IS compared - that is
the part ArchiHUBTestRunner and the Docker healthcheck depend on.
Celery is excluded entirely because worker ping timing is racy.

cases.name: lists: unknown id
cases._note: Legacy returns 200 with an array body here; the port returns 404. Expected - see BACKEND_FINDINGS F13.

cases.name: forms: get one (POST, not GET)
cases._note: Retrieving a form is a POST - FormService.getForm sends POST and expects 200.

cases.name: auth: unknown user is byte-identical to wrong password
_note: Guards the account-enumeration fix: an unknown username and a wrong
password must produce identical responses. ArchiHUBTestRunner asserts
this too; do not 'fix' either side to return 404.
ORDER-DEPENDENT - see _expected_differences.

cases.name: users: me
cases._note: F37: this route lost `requests` to the authentication projection. Diffed here so it cannot happen again.

cases.name: users: me never returns the password hash
_note: `lastRequest` is asserted ABSENT, not present. An earlier revision of
the port added it and `requests` here on a misread harness diff; the
legacy route reaches this through `get_user`, whose projection excludes
both. Adding `lastRequest` also 500'd the route - it is a raw datetime.
The profile screen's quota comes from `/users/requests`; KeysMain.tsx's
only read of `requests` off this response is guarded by `if (...)` and
has always seen it absent.

_comment: The case above omits `type`, so BOTH stacks refuse it and no success
body is ever compared. That is how the payload key silently changed
name here. Send each valid type as well, so the shape is diffed.
cases.name: users: favorites list, resources
users: api keys never return the key itself
_note: New in the port - there is no legacy route to diff against. Keys are
hashed at rest and shown once at creation; a listing that could return
one would defeat the redesign. See API_KEYS_FRONTEND_NOTES.md.

cases.name: system: the bootstrap settings are deliberately anonymous
_note: NOT a 401 case. The login screen reads this before anyone has signed
in, to choose between a login form and the onboarding wizard, so it
has no guard in either stack. It is diffed because every field on it
is public by construction.

cases.name: usertasks: missing both ids is refused
resources: listing
cases._note: F37: this listing lost metadata.firstLevel.title from its projection. Diffed so it cannot recur.

cases.name: resources: listing with the column set the browser actually sends
cases._note: F53. activeColumns is a list of column DESCRIPTORS, not names - the label is what the table header renders. Every earlier listing case omitted the field entirely, so the whole column path went undiffed and the port read the descriptors as strings. Keep the real shape here: a case that sends bare strings agrees with a wrong implementation.

cases.name: resources: listing keeps the title the browse screen renders
cases._note: F37 as a contract, so it outlives legacy.

cases.name: resources: wrong-shaped listing body
cases._note: POST /resources is the multipart CREATE route. A JSON body is a client error; legacy 500s on KeyError 'data', the port answers 422.

cases.name: resources: detail
_note: The detail response is not the document - both detail routes build the
same rendered shape (fields/icon/children/named ancestors). An earlier
version of the port returned the raw document here, which breaks the
detail screen on selectedResource.children.find(...).

cases.name: resources: detail is the rendered shape, not the raw document
resources: public detail is rendered the same way
cases._note: ResourcesService.getOne renders both routes with one component, so both must carry these.

cases.name: resources: public unknown id is 404, not 401
_note: A public route answers 404 for 'not public', byte-identical to 'does
not exist' - an anonymous caller must not have an id confirmed. 401
here would also mean the public router lost its registration-order
precedence to /resources/{resource_id}, which app_factory asserts.

cases.name: records: get by filters
cases._note: `filepath` no longer returned - see _expected_differences.

cases.name: records: the listing does not disclose server paths
cases._note: Two things never leave the records API: filepath and the raw processing block.

cases.name: records: detail does not disclose server paths
records: public detail does not disclose server paths
records: a viewer size outside the allowlist is refused
_note: BACKEND_FINDINGS S18 - arbitrary file read for any authenticated user,
verified resolving to /etc on the legacy stack. `size` indexes a fixed
map and anything not in it is refused before a path is built. A parity
case here would assert the vulnerability.

cases.name: records: a public viewer size outside the allowlist is refused
cases._note: S18 again - the public mirror was equally exposed and unauthenticated.

cases.name: records: a negative page index is refused
cases._note: A negative index must not count back from the end of a document.

cases.name: records: favcount of an unknown record
records: public unknown id is 404, not 401
cases._note: Also proves the public router still mounts before /records/{record_id}.

cases.name: views: the listing never publishes an arbitrary thumbnail
_note: S25 - the legacy models declared filesObj, so editing one field could
publish any image in the archive. GET /views is unauthenticated, so
this is an anonymous exposure. filesObj is absent from CLIENT_FIELDS.

cases.name: geosystem: an object where a string belongs is refused
_note: S27 - both geosystem routes are unauthenticated by design (the explore
map draws before anyone signs in), so the input check IS the injection
defence. Legacy assigned ident into the filter as-is.

cases.name: geosystem: an out-of-range level is refused
search: authenticated
cases._note: Legacy 404s when indexing is off (blueprint never registered); the port answers 503. See _expected_differences. activeColumns carries the column set the browser really sends: `_source` is an allowlist derived from it, so a case that omits it asks for a narrower response than any client ever receives and reports the difference as a regression.

cases.name: search: availability is answered per request, not at construction
_note: ONLY VALID WHILE INDEXING IS OFF on the instance under test - change to
200 once it is on. The point: the route exists either way. Legacy
registered the blueprint at construction, so switching indexing on
meant restarting every worker and the OpenAPI document differed
between instances of the same build.

activeColumns carries the column set the browser really sends: `_source` is an allowlist derived from it, so a case that omits it asks for a narrower response than any client ever receives and reports the difference as a regression.

cases.name: search: a public caller cannot ask for drafts
_note: S28 - DEMONSTRATED on the legacy stack: 16 real drafts returned to an
anonymous caller, because the builder read body['status'] and the
indexer indexes every resource whatever its state. The port decides the
publication state from who is asking and no request field can influence
it. This asserts 503 only because indexing is off on this instance;
with indexing ON, change to 200 and add expect_absent for draft rows.
HOTFIX_S28_legacy.patch is ready for the legacy stack.

activeColumns carries the column set the browser really sends: `_source` is an allowlist derived from it, so a case that omits it asks for a narrower response than any client ever receives and reports the difference as a regression.

cases.name: aiservices: dialects are code, not configuration
_note: aiservices was REWRITTEN, not ported - there is no legacy equivalent to
diff against. A dialect is a wire protocol (a handful exist, they change
over years); a provider is a row in llm_models. This route did not exist
before.

cases.name: aiservices: a provider listing cannot leak a credential
_note: providers.present() is the only serialiser and cannot emit the key - it
returns has_key and a key_fingerprint so two keys can be told apart
without either being seen. The legacy listing shape was a hardcoded
array of vendor names.

cases.name: aiservices: a skill path cannot escape the skills directory
_note: A skill path arrives in a URL and becomes a file that is written, read
and deleted. The legacy check reasoned about the text
(normalized.startswith('..')), which says nothing about symlinks. Every
path goes through core.files.resolve_within instead.

cases.name: aiservices: an absolute skill path is refused, not reinterpreted
adminApi: system info without a Fernet token
adminApi: lookup without a Fernet token
adminApi: a Mongo operator in the lookup body never executes
_note: S29 - the legacy lookup was get_record('resources', body), so this ran
server-side JavaScript. It is an allowlist now (ident, post_type,
metadata.firstLevel.*, string equality only). The token gate answers
first, which is why this asserts 401: the point is that it does NOT
reach the database and does not hang. tests/test_external_api.py
asserts the allowlist itself directly, past the token gate.

cases.name: adminApi: the plugin proxy refuses rather than resolving a path
_note: S30 - the legacy proxy built its target as f'/{plugin}/{endpoint}' from
a path converter, so `..` reached any route in the application, then
re-entered the WSGI stack and copied the inner response's headers out
verbatim. It is an explicit 501 until Phase 5 resolves the target
against the plugin registry. Unauthenticated it is 401, as here.

cases.name: publicApi: listing without a Fernet token
publicApi: types without a Fernet token
publicApi: resource without a Fernet token
system: index maintenance is administrator-only
_note: CONTRACT, NOT PARITY, and deliberately the unauthenticated case: a
parity case here would QUEUE A FULL REINDEX on the shared database, and
an authenticated one would do it twice. What is checkable without
writing anything is that the route exists and refuses - which a route
inventory cannot tell you, because it does not see the guard.
Phase 4. The queued behaviour is covered by tests/test_worker_tasks.py.

cases.name: system: boundary loading is administrator-only
_note: Not fired with a token even at the port: the loader deletes and rewrites
every shape at every administrative level, which is a real write to the
shared database.

cases.name: system: inventory cleanup keeps its underscore path
_note: The path is inconsistent with every neighbour and is kept exactly:
it is the URL the existing frontend calls.

cases.name: plugins: liquidText generation needs a role
_note: CONTRACT, and the unauthenticated case throughout this group. A plugin
route with a token would queue real work against the shared database,
and firing it at both backends would queue it twice.
What these DO establish is BACKEND_FINDINGS S32: the legacy framework's
validate_roles returned a refusal tuple that all eleven of its call
sites discarded, so those routes were guarded by nothing but a valid
session. In the port the role is a dependency - there is no return
value to drop - and that is what a 401 here demonstrates end to end.

cases.name: plugins: liquidText save needs a role
plugins: liquidText export needs a role
plugins: filesProcessing bulk needs a role
plugins: inventoryMaker bulk needs a role
plugins: massiveUpdater launch needs a role
plugins: settings cannot be read without a role
plugins: settings cannot be written without a role
_note: The scheduleSystemTasks equivalent is the sharpest case in this group -
its settings ARE a task scheduler, so writing them makes the workers run
something repeatedly. It is not listed because that plugin is not active
on this instance; filesProcessing exercises the same shared route.

cases.name: plugins: the icon needs a role
plugins: task results need a role
plugins: the public inventory refuses a request naming no view
_note: Deliberately malformed, so it is refused BEFORE anything is generated -
the route is unauthenticated and does write a workbook to the web files
volume when it succeeds.
The behaviour that changed and is NOT covered here is S33: the legacy
filter was content type plus published status and nothing else, so a
resource under embargo appeared in an inventory anyone could download.
Verifying that needs an instance with a reserved resource in a public
view; tests/test_plugin_framework.py covers the rule itself.

cases.name: system: the actions menu needs a role
types: info-panel timeCreated statistics
cases._note: Read-only aggregation. Ported late (the route was missing from the port entirely, so Info.tsx got a 405); diffed against legacy because both stacks have it.

cases.name: types: info-panel statusCount statistics
cases._note: Read-only aggregation. Ported late (the route was missing from the port entirely, so Info.tsx got a 405); diffed against legacy because both stacks have it.

cases.name: types: info-panel authorCount statistics
cases._note: Read-only aggregation. Ported late (the route was missing from the port entirely, so Info.tsx got a 405); diffed against legacy because both stacks have it.

cases.name: types: an unknown chart is answered ok, not an error
cases._note: The panel asks for several charts by name; one the backend does not recognise must not fail the screen.

cases.name: system: the plugin listing carries every field /processing renders
cases._note: Contract, not parity: legacy returns each plugin's whole `plugin_info`, the port a chosen subset. `type` is what /processing maps over to build its buttons and route to /processing/{type}/{slug}; omitting it crashed the page on undefined.map. `plugins` guards F38, where the payload was a bare array.

cases.name: records: an image record is servable by the document reader
cases._note: `ImageViewer.tsx` calls the shared viewer's `init` with four arguments, so `isDocument` keeps its default and the body carries `gallery: false`. Refusing here while `/document` answers {"pages": 1} leaves the reader knowing about a page it can never fetch.

cases.name: records: an image page carries the aspect ratio the reader draws from
records: a traversing size is refused on an image record too
cases._note: S18. Serving images from this route must not turn the size check into a pass-through.

cases.name: records: EXIF never states where the file lives
cases._note: The presentable EXIF subset is an allowlist. `File:Directory`/`SourceFile` are the server's own paths arriving through a second door - the one thing this API goes out of its way never to return.

cases.name: aiservices: a provider's detail cannot leak its credential
cases._note: present() is the only serialiser and it cannot emit the key. `has_key` and `key_fingerprint` exist so two keys can be told apart without either being seen; asserting they are PRESENT keeps a future 'just drop the field' fix from passing the absence check while removing the operator's only way to tell which key is stored.

cases.name: aiservices: the model catalogue cannot leak a credential
cases._note: This route round-trips through the vendor. `expect_absent` walks every nesting level, so a key echoed back inside a model's `metadata` is caught too.

cases.name: aiservices: the reachability check reports without leaking
cases._note: Discovery failure must be REPORTED, never papered over - legacy returned a hardcoded model list when getModels raised, so a provider with an expired key showed a normal catalogue of models that could not be called.

cases.name: aiservices: a provider's detail needs a token
aiservices: the model catalogue needs a token
cases._note: Unauthenticated reachability probing against the operator's own vendor account, billed to them, is the thing to keep shut.

cases.name: aiservices: the reachability check needs a token
aiservices: conversation history answers a bare array
cases._note: F66. `AImessaging.tsx` does `Array.isArray(response) ? response : []`, so an envelope reads as NO RESULTS - a 200 that renders 'No results' for a user who has conversations. The status alone cannot see it; this case exists so the shape is asserted even when the instance has none for this record.

cases.name: aiservices: conversation history needs a token
aiservices: an unknown conversation is 404, not someone else's
cases._note: A conversation belongs to the person who had it. The legacy delete filtered on the id alone, so a known id deleted anyone's; the read is guarded by the same load_own.

cases.name: aiservices: reading a conversation needs a token
records: the media stream serves bytes to a permitted caller
cases._note: Range support comes from Starlette's FileResponse, so the players' seeking needs no custom code - but only if the route actually serves the file. Binary, so this asserts rather than diffs.

cases.name: records: the media stream needs a token
cases._note: The authenticated stream is the one route that hands over the stored bytes directly; the public mirror is a separate path with its own is_public rule.

cases.name: plugins: a plugin's settings need a token
plugins: a plugin's settings are readable by a permitted caller
cases._note: The processing screen renders its form from this. S32's fix made every plugin role check a dependency rather than a discarded return value, so a route that used to be guarded by nothing now refuses - this asserts it did not overshoot into refusing everyone.

cases.name: plugins: a plugin declaring no settings is 404, not a traceback
cases._note: Legacy answers 500 here for both inventoryMaker and massiveUpdater, which declare no settings block.

cases.name: plugins: a plugin icon needs a token
adminApi: get_type refuses without a Fernet token
cases._note: The external APIs are consumed by other organisations' scripts, so their guards are invisible to any upgrade_front audit.

cases.name: records: the public stream refuses a non-media record with a reason
cases._note: Legacy answers 500 with the same message. Anonymous, so the refusal must be a refusal and not a traceback.

cases.name: plugins: the inventoryMaker icon needs a token
plugins: the massiveUpdater icon needs a token
cases._note: Each plugin declares its own routes, so the guard is asserted per plugin rather than assumed from the framework - S32 was 21 call sites that each looked fine on their own.

cases.name: plugins: massiveUpdater settings need a role
_note: CONTRACT. The settings routes every plugin gets for free were the only
reachable plugin GETs with no case at all - a read, so the harness can
fire it, unlike the plugin's write routes.

cases.name: plugins: massiveUpdater result download needs a role
_note: CONTRACT, and the guard is what matters: the task id is deliberately one
that does not exist, so a 401 proves the role is resolved BEFORE the task
is looked up. A 404 here would mean an anonymous caller can probe which
task ids exist.

_expected_differences: Parity cases that differ ON PURPOSE. Re-triaged 2026-08-19 against both
running backends, with the three legacy hotfixes (S18/S28/S31) applied and
every fixture resolving - so for the first time NOTHING is skipped and the
public routes are exercised against genuinely public data.
-- the port returns the right code where legacy faults --
types: unknown slug            legacy 500 -> 404
users: unknown id              legacy 500 (leaks the bson InvalidId text) -> 404
users: favorites list, missing type   legacy 500 (KeyError 'type') -> 422
lists: unknown id              legacy 200 carrying a 500-shaped body -> 404
logs: list                     legacy 500 -> 200
tasks: list                    legacy 500 (the handler returns None, which
Flask reports as an invalid response) -> 200
resources: wrong-shaped body   legacy 500 (KeyError 'data') -> 422
resources: favcount            legacy 500 -> 200
records: favcount (both)       legacy 500 / wrongly-200 -> 200 / 404
records: transcription (both)  legacy 500 -> 400 naming the missing field
geosystem: polygon             legacy 404 -> 400 with a reason
-- legacy defects the harness surfaced, recorded in BACKEND_FINDINGS --
records: public page images    legacy 500s unconditionally - it calls
public_services.get_document_pages, which does
not exist. The public document viewer has never
worked. The port returns the pages. (F41)
resources: public listing      legacy 401s the WHOLE request when any one of
the requested types declares viewRoles, so the
public explore screen is dead for any mixed
selection. The port serves the types that are
public and omits the rest.
-- the public rule, applied where legacy over-discloses (S20) --
Legacy serves a record to an anonymous caller on the strength of the record
alone. The port requires the whole ancestry to be public: published,
unrestricted after inheritance, and the content type declaring no viewRoles.
Demonstrated live on this instance, not reasoned about - record
69028a22334c67f3a123b145 is filed under three `casos` resources, TWO OF THEM
DRAFTS, and `casos` declares viewRoles ['user']. Legacy answers 200 to a
caller with no token; the port answers 404. The public cases now resolve
their fixtures THROUGH the public listing so they exercise the response
rather than the refusal - pointing them at an id from the authenticated
listing tested the refusal while looking like it tested the document.
-- deliberate shape changes --
records: get by filters        `filepath` no longer returned
records: detail (both)         adds `mime`/`status`; drops a parent's
`accessRights: null` (absent vs null); EXIF is
reduced to the presentable subset, which drops
GPS, serial numbers, owner names AND
`File:Directory`/`SourceFile` - the server's own
paths, arriving through a second door
views: detail                  adds `id` alongside `_id` (additive)
search: * (authenticated)      adds `status` (additive). The port's `_source`
is an allowlist, so a case must send the
`activeColumns` a browser really sends or it
asks for less than any client receives - the
cases now do
users: request quota           legacy returned the raw document (`_id`,
`lastRequest`); the port returns
{requests, limit}
users: list all                `createdAt` is an HTTP date where legacy
emitted {"$date": ...}. No caller reads it -
the admin users table does not render the
column - and the two date conventions are both
wire contract, chosen per route. Contrast
`tasks`, where the panel DOES read `.$date` and
the port was corrected to match.
forms: unknown slug            same 404, different message text
records: public gallery info   same 400, different message text
search: public rss             same 400, different message text
-- availability is answered per request, not at construction --
search: *                      legacy registers the blueprint only when
indexing is on; the port always registers and
answers 503 when it is off. Indexing is ON on
this instance, so the two contract cases
asserting 503 report 200/403 instead. They are
asserting the OTHER configuration and are only
meaningful on an instance without Elasticsearch.
adminApi/publicApi: *          same, for `api_activation`. It is ON here, so
the two adminApi contract cases expecting the
switched-off 404 get 401 - the API is on and is
asking who they are. Where both stacks do answer
404, only the body differs: legacy serves
Werkzeug's HTML, the port serves JSON that is
byte-identical to its own unrouted-path 404,
which is the property that matters.
-- plugin scope, and a real cutover consequence --
system: plugins                Both stacks scan a plugins directory; they scan
DIFFERENT ONES. Legacy lists the 22 directories
under app/plugins, the port the five under
archihub/plugins, plus anything active in either
case. So the difference is which plugins are
installed where, not a rule about which names
are permitted - copy a plugin into the port's
directory and it is listed and activatable with
no change to this backend.
FOR THE OPERATOR RELEASE NOTES: a plugin written
against Flask stays listed after cutover but is
marked unsupported and carries the reason, and
activating it is refused explicitly rather than
failing obscurely at the next restart.
The port also adds `installed` and `problem`, and
drops `settings`, `actions` and `capabilities` -
none of which is read from this route by any
caller. `PluginsResults.tsx` and
`processing/page.tsx` use only slug, name,
description, active and type; settings come from
the plugin's own /settings route.
plugins: liquidText *          liquidText is INACTIVE on this instance, so its
routes are not mounted and answer 404 where the
case expects the 401 of a mounted, guarded
route. Environmental: activate it to exercise
these.
-- order-dependent --
auth: byte-identical           passes alone; in a full run the port's login
throttle (S2, which legacy lacks) trips and
the statuses diverge. Run it with
--only byte-identical, or after a Redis flush.
